title: US hack into our health records
full_text:
A US-based hacker has claimed responsibility for breaching a NSW Health database and successfully stealing sensitive files related to an unclear number of private dentist clinics across the state.
According to Hackmanac, a verified X thread which tracks illegal data breaches, a hacker who works under the tag ‘bytetobreach’ has claimed to have pillaged around 100,000 documents from NSW Health.
Internal NSW Health systems detected unusual activity last Friday, and within three hours NSW Police had begun investigating the activity as a major data breach at the hands of international actors.
The hacker has claimed to have stolen around 70 gigabytes of data, but NSW Police say it’s more like four gigabytes.
Chief executive of eHealth NSW, Richard Taggart, said the incident had targeted the ‘oral health fee-for-service’ website, which allows people to apply for vouchers from NSW Health so they can pay for dental work.
“There’s no patient data involved at all in this circumstance. It’s only a small number of third party provider data that we look at,” he said.
NSW Police Cyber Crime Squad Commander Matt Craft didn’t confirm whether police were focusing specifically on Bytetobreach, but did say the US hacker was well-known to the Cyber Crime Squad, describing them as “a nuisance” who had previously made false claims. “We’re aware of certain posts that have been made and that will form part of our criminal investigation,” Supt Craft said.
“Just because somebody is posting something online using a handle, doesn’t make it true. We need to assess that.” Supt Craft said there was an “international flavour” to the investigation, and NSW Police have engaged with US Homeland Security and the FBI.
